headline: North Korea Fires Ballistic Missile From Wonsan Toward East Sea
seoTitle: North Korea Missile Flies Over 700 km From Wonsan | FMB News
seoDescription: South Korea says North Korea’s ballistic missile flew more than 700 kilometers from Wonsan; Japan says it landed outside its exclusive economic zone.
deck: South Korea says the missile flew more than 700 kilometers from Wonsan; Japan says it landed outside its exclusive economic zone, while the model and altitude remain undisclosed.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What is confirmed
paragraphs: South Korea’s Joint Chiefs of Staff said a ballistic missile launched from North Korea’s eastern coastal Wonsan area flew more than 700 kilometers toward the East Sea on Saturday. South Korean and U.S. militaries were analyzing the weapon’s specifics.

Japan’s Defense Ministry said the missile landed outside Japan’s exclusive economic zone. South Korea said it increased surveillance for possible additional launches and continued sharing information with the United States and Japan.

sections.heading: How the report changed
paragraphs: FMB News first published the launch as an unidentified projectile because the initial military notice had not established the weapon type. The article was updated when South Korea classified it as a ballistic missile, and is now updated again with the confirmed flight distance and Japan’s reported landing assessment.
The missile’s specific model, maximum altitude and exact impact point remain undisclosed in the reviewed material. North Korean state media had not issued a claim about the launch.

sections.heading: Why it matters to Filipinos
paragraphs: A ballistic-missile launch on the Korean Peninsula can affect regional security, aviation or maritime warnings and the safety outlook for Filipinos living and working in South Korea and Japan.
No immediate threat to the Philippines or disruption to Filipino communities was reported.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch for a fuller South Korean or Japanese tracking assessment, a North Korean state-media claim and any aviation or maritime safety notice.
Seoul’s presidential national security office called for North Korea to halt repeated ballistic launches, describing them as violations of United Nations Security Council resolutions.

verificationNotes: The Joint Chiefs of Staff is the official issuing authority; AP’s updated report attributes the more-than-700-kilometer flight assessment directly to the South Korean military.
AP separately attributes the outside-EEZ landing assessment to Japan’s Defense Ministry.
The article preserves the chronology of the initial unidentified-projectile report and later ballistic-missile classification rather than rewriting the uncertainty out of the record.
Missile model, maximum altitude and exact impact point remain unresolved in the reviewed material.
No documentary launch image with verified reusable rights was available; FMB’s owned fallback is clearly labeled non-documentary.
